lessons.topic: Oral – Written — Say and recognize the numbers from 11 to 20 (diagnostic assessment)
objectives: By the end of the lesson, my learners will be able to say and recognize the numbers from 11 to 20 (diagnostic assessment).
Lexis: eleven, twelve, … , twenty.
lessons.body:
Domain: Oral – Written
Objective: By the end of the lesson, my learners will be able to say and recognize the numbers from 11 to 20 (diagnostic assessment).

Lexis: eleven, twelve, … , twenty.
Materials: Textbook (p. 6), number cards.

▪ Warming up (2-5m): The teacher greets learners and welcomes them. 1, 2, 3. Learn English with me!
   Greetings and short revision of the numbers 0–10 learnt in 3PS.
   [T.SS / S.SS]
▪ Presentation (8-10m): T. presents the numbers 11–20 with number cards; PP listen and repeat (chorally then individually).
   [T.SS / SS.T]
▪ Practice (15-20m): Task One (Listen and repeat the numbers 11–20): T. points at a number, PP say it; then a pupil says it, another one shows it.
   [T.S / S.S]
▪ Use/produce (8-10m): Game “Number chain”: PP count from 11 to 20 and then backwards.
   Use this lesson as a diagnostic assessment: note who recognizes the numbers.
   [S.S / SS.T]

lessons.body:
Domain: Oral – Written
Objective: By the end of the lesson, my learners will be able to read a short text about a family and pronounce /θ/ and /ð/ in family words.
Target structures: This is my aunt. She is my mother’s sister. She is 30.
Lexis: grandfather, grandmother, aunt, mother’s sister, thirty, three, father, mother, brother, this.
Materials: Textbook (p. 11–12), phonics cards, copybook.

▪ Warming up (2-5m): The teacher greets learners and welcomes them. 1, 2, 3. Learn English with me!
   Review of the previous lesson (flash and say).
   [T.SS / S.SS]
▪ Presentation (8-10m): I read and discover: T. reads the text (“Hi, welcome to my home! This is my family…”); PP listen, then read aloud.
   Phonics (Read and repeat the words): three – thirty (/θ/) and father – mother – brother – this (/ð/).
   [T.SS / SS.T]

   Task Two (Read the text and match the pairs, page 12):
   Key: 1 mother’s parents = b grandparents – 2 mother’s sister = a aunt – 3 Souad = d grandmother – 4 thirty = c 30.
   Task Three: complete the family tree of Nadjib; draw your own family tree.
   [T.S / S.S]

Target structures: Where is the gorilla? – It is …
Lexis: bear, kangaroo, elephant, giraffe, gazelle, monkey, hippopotamus, crocodile, gorilla.
lessons.body:
Domain: Oral
Objective: By the end of the lesson, my learners will be able to recognize and say the names of zoo animals.
Target structures: Where is the gorilla? – It is …
Lexis: bear, kangaroo, elephant, giraffe, gazelle, monkey, hippopotamus, crocodile, gorilla.
Materials: Textbook (p. 87–89), zoo flashcards, audio.

▪ Warming up (2-5m): The teacher greets learners and welcomes them. 1, 2, 3. Learn English with me!
   Review of the previous lesson (flash and say).
   [T.SS / S.SS]
▪ Presentation (8-10m): T. presents the zoo animals with flashcards; PP repeat. Song: “Baa Baa Black Sheep”.
   [T.SS / SS.T]
▪ Practice (15-20m): I listen and repeat. #Task One (page 88): listen and put a cross on the right box.
   Page 89: listen and locate the gorilla and the monkeys.
   Answers from the audio script.
   [T.S / S.S]
▪ Use/produce (8-10m): Game “Which animal am I?” (mime).
   [S.S / SS.T]

lessons.topic: Oral – Written — Read about wild animals and pronounce /ɜː/ (bird, turkey)
objectives: By the end of the lesson, my learners will be able to read about wild animals and pronounce /ɜː/ (bird, turkey).
Target structures: The tiger, the lion, the fox and the wolf are carnivores. They eat meat. The elephant, the giraffe and the gazelle are herbivores. They eat grass and fruits.
Lexis: tiger, lion, fox, wolf, elephant, giraffe, gazelle, turkey, bird, girl, turtle; carnivores, herbivores, meat, grass, fruits, grains.
lessons.body:
Domain: Oral – Written
Objective: By the end of the lesson, my learners will be able to read about wild animals and pronounce /ɜː/ (bird, turkey).
Target structures: The tiger, the lion, the fox and the wolf are carnivores. They eat meat. The elephant, the giraffe and the gazelle are herbivores. They eat grass and fruits.
Lexis: tiger, lion, fox, wolf, elephant, giraffe, gazelle, turkey, bird, girl, turtle; carnivores, herbivores, meat, grass, fruits, grains.
Materials: Textbook (p. 90–92), copybook.

▪ Warming up (2-5m): The teacher greets learners and welcomes them. 1, 2, 3. Learn English with me!
   Review of the previous lesson (flash and say).
   [T.SS / S.SS]
▪ Presentation (8-10m): I read and discover: T. reads the text; PP read aloud.
   Phonics: bird – turkey – girl – turtle.
   [T.SS / SS.T]
▪ Practice (15-20m): Task One: circle the words with the same sound as “bird”.
   Task Two: match the words that have the same sound as “bird” (turkey, journey, kangaroo …).
   Task Three: cross the odd animal out (rhinoceros – sheep – gazelle – lion).
   Task Four: identify the animals in the word search.
   [T.S / S.S]
▪ Use/produce (8-10m): PP say what an animal eats: “The lion eats meat.”
   [S.S / SS.T]

Domain: Written

Target structures: Nadjib is watching the tiger. Massil is feeding the gazelle. Mustapha is taking photos of the lion.
Lexis: watching, feeding, taking photos, tiger, gazelle, lion.
Materials: Textbook (p. 93–94), copybook.

▪ Warming up (2-5m): The teacher greets learners and welcomes them. 1, 2, 3. Learn English with me!
   Review of the previous lesson (flash and say).
   [T.SS / S.SS]
▪ Presentation (8-10m): I read and write: T. reads the text; PP read aloud.
   [T.SS / SS.T]
▪ Practice (15-20m): Task One: copy and complete the table: Nadjib – watching the tiger; Massil – feeding the gazelle; Mustapha – taking photos of the lion.

lessons.topic: Oral – Written — Use the language of the sequence (assessment, remediation and standardization)
objectives: By the end of the lesson, my learners will be able to use the language of the sequence (assessment, remediation and standardization).
Target structures: Structures of the sequence.
Lexis: Lexis of the sequence.
lessons.body:
Domain: Oral – Written
Objective: By the end of the lesson, my learners will be able to use the language of the sequence (assessment, remediation and standardization).
Target structures: Structures of the sequence.
Lexis: Lexis of the sequence.
Materials: Worksheets, flashcards, copybook.

▪ Warming up (2-5m): The teacher greets learners and welcomes them. 1, 2, 3. Learn English with me!
   Quick review of the sequence with flashcards.
   [T.SS / S.SS]
▪ Presentation (8-10m): Assessment:
   Listening: T. says words or sentences from the sequence; PP tick, match or circle.
   Speaking: PP ask and answer in pairs using the structures of the sequence.
   Reading/writing: read a short text, complete a table, reorder words, copy a sentence.
   Adapt the tasks to what has actually been taught in your class.
   [T.S / S]
▪ Practice (15-20m): Remediation: T. corrects the common mistakes on the board; weaker learners work in small groups with flashcards while the others play a game.
   [T.S / S.S]
▪ Use/produce (8-10m): Standardization: PP consolidate through a game or a mini-dialogue with a partner, then say what they have learnt.
   [S.S / SS.T]
